You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_target.csv: 284 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, whose rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) is AS CLOSE AS POSSIBLE
to 800. Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning

**Data structure.** The dataset splits into two regimes:

1. **Through-hardened Q&T steels** (CT=30, Ct=0, Dt=0, TT=490–680): targets 325–718 MPa.
2. **Carburized steels** (CT=930, Ct>0, Dt>0, TT=160–200): targets 900–1190 MPa.

There is a **gap between 718 and 900 MPa**, so hitting 800 requires interpolating trends. The closest real sample is 718 MPa (NT=845, THT=845, TT=490, C=0.62, Cr=0.75). I will push this Q&T recipe upward rather than try to soften a carburized part (carburizing trends are noisier and start 100+ MPa above target).

**Key trends in the Q&T regime:**
- **Tempering temperature TT** is the strongest lever: within matched groups, dropping TT by 50 °C raises strength ~25–40 MPa (e.g., 650→600→550 series). The 718 MPa sample used TT=490; going lower (~450–460, still within the allowed [30,680]) should gain ~+25–35 MPa.
- **Carbon**: higher C consistently raises strength (0.32→0.57 gives ~+50–80 MPa within groups). Use C=0.63 (max).
- **Cr ≈ 1.0** vs Cr ≈ 0.1 groups (855-THT series vs 845/825) shows ~+70–100 MPa at same TT. Use Cr=1.1.
- **Mo ≈ 0.15–0.2** appears in the higher-strength Q&T samples (adds tempering resistance). Use Mo=0.18.
- **Low inclusions/defects** (small dA, dB, dC; low P, S) correlate with higher fatigue strength → set near-zero defects, low P/S.
- Keep Mn ~0.8, Si ~0.3, moderate RedRatio (~820) as in high-strength samples.

Stacking: 718 (base) + ~30 (TT 490→455) + ~50 (Cr 0.75→1.1, Mo added) + ~10 (cleaner steel, zero defects) ≈ **~800 MPa**, without leaving observed variable ranges.

Process columns follow the Q&T template: NT=845, THT=845, THt=30, THQCr=8, no carburizing/diffusion (CT=30, Ct=0, DT=30, Dt=0, QmT=30), temper Tt=60, TCr=24.

## Proposal

Final: NT=845, THT=845, THt=30, THQCr=8, CT=30, Ct=0, DT=30, Dt=0, QmT=30, TT=455, Tt=60, TCr=24, C=0.63, Si=0.3, Mn=0.85, P=0.01, S=0.005, Ni=0.1, Cr=1.1, Cu=0.12, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=820, dA=0.0, dB=0.0, dC=0.0
